The GSO verifier reported binary_reward 0 with continuous reward 0.602 and opt_commit false [1], and passing requires reward strictly above 1.2 on the gm_speedup_patch_commit metric [2]. The attempt was directionally right and materially faster than baseline on test 0, but it is not the reference-quality optimization this task gates on, so TN is the right classification.

The GSO verifier compared the agent patch against baseline and reference commit bfaf917 ("PERF: Avoid np.divmod in maybe_sequence_to_range") across 20 held-out workloads, reported opt_commit=False with continuous reward 0.483, and applied a pass threshold of 1.2 that the patch did not meet [1][2][3][4]. The agent instead iterated on pure-Python early exits—ndarray fast path, cached scalars, and adjacent-difference rejection—but left np.divmod in the hot path [6][7]. The agent declared success after local timing on only the random-input scenario (~1e-6s median) and 195 self-generated equivalence cases, without measuring performance on range-convertible inputs where divmod dominates [10]. Correctness was preserved (all eqchecks passed), but for this continuous-reward GSO task that is insufficient: the patch is roughly half the speed of the reference commit overall and does not meet the required threshold, so it was not truly solved [1][2][8].

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure on a continuous-reward GSO task—the verifier correctly rejected the rollout. The harness reported opt_commit=False with geometric-mean speedup gm_speedup_patch_commit=0.727, below the pass gate of reward>1.2 [1][2][3], yielding binary_reward=0 [1]. The instruction asked to optimize maybe_sequence_to_range while preserving functional equivalence across general workloads, not just the toy random-int benchmark [4]. The hidden reference at commit bfaf917d2c replaces np.divmod with a new Cython lib.is_sequence_range that validates arithmetic sequences in an allocation-free C loop [5][6], whereas the agent's final patch only adds an O(1) endpoint rejection fast-path and swaps divmod for (np.diff(np_sequence)==diff).all() in pandas/core/indexes/base.py [7][8]. That approach is functionally correct—the verifier's 20 equivalence checks all passed [9]—and it crushes the instruction's random-input benchmark (test 0 drops from ~9ms to ~0.02ms) [9][10], but on convertible-range workloads like gso_test_1's million-element arange the patch still runs a full np.diff (~0.0023s) while the reference commit runs in ~0.0006s [9][11], dragging the aggregate score to 0.73× the reference. The agent declared success after self-tests focused on the prompt's random-data scenario and a handful of hand cases, without probing valid-range paths where its numpy diff validation loses to the reference [12][13][10]. Because the task gates on matching or exceeding the reference optimization level and the agent materially underperforms it, the verifier FAIL is correct and this is TN, not FN.
